title: Handoff Saga: Incremental Deploy & Compatibility Notes
content:
Purpose and framing:
This doc captures an experimental "handoff saga" approach for moving Private deployments (VPC / on-prem appliances) from one runtime+control-plane combination to another with minimal user-visible disruption. The aim is to codify a sequence of small, reversible stateful operations (compensating steps) across control-plane and runtime, plus an automated verification surface.

Why "saga" here?
- We have multiple orthogonal state machines: TF state, control-plane leader maps, runtime node binary versions, KV schemas and client API contracts.
- A monolithic cutover is risky; instead, treat the transition as a distributed transaction implemented via a saga: each step has a forward action and an explicit compensating (undo) action.

High-level phases (incremental):
1) Preflight lab and shadowing
   - Create a staging replica of customer's TF state in the lab: terraform state pull -> apply to isolated overlay workspace.
   - Start a shadow control-plane (read-only leader candidates) running new control-plane that pulls real telemetry but does not accept production writes.
   - Run traffic replay from recorded traces for 24–72h.
   - Acceptance criteria: no unhandled 5xxs; request/response invariants match within threshold.

2) Compatibility shims and API gating
   - Deploy a transparent API shim sidecar at the ingress of the runtime nodes that can translate new control-plane responses to legacy client expectations (and vice-versa).
   - Expose a /compatibility/probe endpoint that returns a pass/fail matrix.
   - Test matrix includes: session handshake, model invocation signatures, tokenizable metadata, streaming chunk boundaries.

3) Canary cohort (in-situ small % of production)
   - Select low-QPS tenants (single-region, low-latency slack teams) to route via the new control-plane + runtime variant.
   - Execution pattern: route 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% over a 48–96h window, with automated rollback on metric breach.
   - Key SLOs to monitor: tail P95 latency, token error-rate, inference mismatch rate (compared vs baseline), KV cache hit regression.

4) Stateful migration windows (KV / prefix caches / stored sessions)
   - Introduce a dual-write mode for session and small KV (writes happen to both runtimes), with reads optionally configured to prefer legacy until warmed.
   - Run background reconciliation jobs that rebase and replay prefix caches into the new runtime using customer-approved sample prompts.
   - Reconciliation acceptance: less than X% mismatches after Y runs (tunable per-customer).

5) Broad rollout and final cutover
   - Once metrics are stable for multiple cohorts and reconciliation pass rates are within tolerance, shift control-plane leadership and optionally retire legacy control-plane in waves.
   - Final pass: cut TF pins (if pinned) and converge to a single canonical state. Keep snapshot for 30 days before purge.

Compensating actions (examples):
- If canary inference mismatch > threshold -> toggle canary routing back, drain new runtime nodes (no new sessions), and schedule compensating reconciliation job to replay the mismatched requests.
- If TF drift detected (state file checksum mismatch) -> lock downstream automation and run a guided delta apply on an isolated control-plane to reproduce and reconcile; if irrecoverable, revert to last good TF snapshot.
- If shim translation produces data loss -> enable payload-capture on the edge and re-run a fixup pass through the legacy runtime with captured payloads.

Terraform and artifact handling notes:
- Strategy: add an overlay workspace (terraform workspace "handoff-<customer>-<date>") rather than in-place mutation. Overlay contains only ephemeral resources (bastions, mirror control-plane lb).
- Keep resource addresses stable (avoid renaming modules) to make state mv operations minimal. When address change is unavoidable, perform explicit terraform state mv steps documented in the runbook.
- Example sequence: state pull -> terraform workspace new -> terraform import LB and mirror nodes -> smoke apply -> terraform state push (to overlay).

Verification harness (automation):
- smoke-checker: small binary that runs a fixed set of API handshakes and stores canonical outputs. Always run before/after each step.
- parity-checker: offline job that samples N requests and compares new-runtime outputs to baseline. Attach threshold and Anomaly scoring.
- replay-runner: replays captured traffic (optionally rate-limited) into the new runtime.

Telemetry and SLO gating:
- Required dashboards before canary: token-error-rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, model-output-diff-rate, kv-hit-rate, tail-kv-stalls, API-500 count.
- Build an automated gate: if any of these crosses configured threshold for > 10m -> auto-rollback trigger and paging to oncall.

Rollback play examples (saga compensating flow):
1) Canary fails at 20% step:
   - Toggle traffic back to legacy via routing control-plane policy (compensating action).
   - Mark canary hosts CORDONED; collect core dumps and attach to Jira PD-8672.
   - Run targeted reconciliation on lost prefix caches, rehydrate if feasible.
2) Mid-migration TF state corruption:
   - Immediately freeze automation (apply-lock), restore last good TF snapshot into overlay, and trigger an out-of-band reconciliation.
   - Notify legal/security if state included customer secrets outside expected KMS envelope.

Checklist for each incremental window (template):
- [ ] TF overlay workspace created + snapshot saved
- [ ] Staging control-plane running and health=green for 12h
- [ ] Shim sidecar deployed and probe=pass
- [ ] Smoke-checker baseline vs new runtime pass
- [ ] Canary group selected and informed (internal CS sync)
- [ ] Telemetry gates configured + alerts enabled
- [ ] Rollback procedure validated in lab (time-to-fallback < 5m)
- [ ] Post-cutover snapshot retention policy applied

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- Create workspace: terraform workspace new handoff-ACME-20251102
- Pull state: terraform state pull > state.json.backup
- Import mirror LB: terraform import module.mirror.aws_lb mirror-lb-abc123
- Run smoke-checker (local): ./smoke-checker --target https://mirror-controlplane.internal --suite handshake,model-call

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How long to keep dual-write mode on by default? (30 days nominal, but customers with heavy sessionization may need 60–90.)
- Failure taxonomy: define what exactly counts as a "mismatch" for auto-rollback vs "degraded" for manual review.
- Who signs off final TF state convergence for enterprise customers (AE + Security + Infra)?

Postmortem and learning capture:
- Every incremental window gets a short postmortem template: what happened, root cause, partial mitigations, followups (owners + dates), and a short replay of traffic artifacts used. Store artifacts in GCS under /private-deployments/handoff-saga/%CUSTOMER%/%DATE%/

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Wire an internal CLI that can perform the entire saga step atomically (start-step, verify-step, commit-step, compensating-step).
- Add a minimal GUI in Console for teams to watch handoff progress and initiate manual compensations.
_comments: internal draft — experimental pattern (not yet approved for enterprise production). Keep small team loop until validated with 3 customers.
